stemBlocks.value: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB, E lies on AC and DE is parallel to BC, with AD = 6 cm, DB = 4 cm and AE = 7.5 cm. a) Explain why triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC. b) Calculate the length of EC. c) The area of triangle ADE is 27 cm². Calculate the area of trapezium DBCE.
Think first: DE parallel to BC creates equal corresponding angles, which is exactly what similarity needs — and remember the sides are compared to the whole triangle, not to the small piece.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p167-q07 from workbook page 167.

solutionSteps.instruction: Match the angles of the two triangles.

contentBlocks.value: ∠ADE = ∠ABC and ∠AED = ∠ACB (corresponding angles, DE parallel to BC); ∠A is common

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the ratio of corresponding sides using the full side AB.
Convert the length ratio to an area ratio.

contentBlocks.value: Area ADE : area ABC = 3² : 5² = 9 : 25, so area ABC = 27 × 25/9
Area DBCE = area ABC − area ADE = 75 − 27

strategyBlocks.value: Establish AA similarity from the parallel lines, use the ratio AD : AB to find AC and then EC, and square the length ratio to compare areas.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) ∠A is common and ∠ADE = ∠ABC, ∠AED = ∠ACB are corresponding angles because DE is parallel to BC, so the triangles are similar by AA  (b) EC = 5 cm  (c) area of trapezium DBCE = 48 cm²

whyThisWorks.value: Parallel lines force corresponding angles to be equal, so the small triangle is an exact scaled copy of the large one sitting in the same corner. Under a scale factor k every length multiplies by k but every area multiplies by k², because area depends on two perpendicular directions at once. That is why a 3 : 5 length ratio becomes a 9 : 25 area ratio, and the trapezium is simply what is left when the small triangle is removed.

commonErrors.misconception: Using AD : DB = 6 : 4 as the scale factor instead of AD : AB = 6 : 10.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using AD : DB = 6 : 4 as the scale factor instead of AD : AB = 6 : 10.

commonErrors.misconception: Scaling the area by 3/5 rather than (3/5)².
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Scaling the area by 3/5 rather than (3/5)².

commonErrors.misconception: Giving the area of the whole triangle ABC as the answer to part c instead of subtracting the small triangle.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Giving the area of the whole triangle ABC as the answer to part c instead of subtracting the small triangle.

examTip.value: In a 'triangle within a triangle' similarity, always write out the full side of the large triangle first (AB = AD + DB) — the single most common error is comparing a part to a part.
